pool.text: Mission San Xavier del Bac was founded by Italian Jesuit missionary Eusebio Francisco Kino.
Hugo O'Conor authorized the construction of Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón as a fort.
Tucson was included in Sonora after Mexico gained independence from the Spanish Empire.
The United States acquired southern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico under the Gadsden Purchase.
Weekly Arizonian, the state's first newspaper, was founded in this year.
Tucson served as the capital of the Arizona Territory until a later year.
The Tucson Symphony Orchestra was founded to provide musical organizations for the city.
Centennial Hall opened as the campus auditorium of the University of Arizona.
Tucson High School achieved the largest secondary school enrollment in the United States.
The Sundt operating station has been online generating air pollution since this year.
El Tucsonense, a Spanish language paper, became defunct in this year.
Tucson and Pima County adopted dark sky ordinances to control light pollution.
The El Tour de Tucson cycling race took place for the first time.
The local transit system was awarded Best Transit System during this year.
The first All Souls Procession was organized by local artist Susan Kay Johnson.
Tucson was dubbed Optics Valley when a cover story was published.
Tucson Water delivered unacceptable CAP water to some customers due to quality issues.
CAP water enabled the city to remove or turn off numerous wells.
Tucson became the first city in the state to pass a domestic partnership registry.
A contract was awarded to SunEdison to construct a large PV field.
